builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Guided Generation of Linux Kernel Semantic Patches with Small Local Language Models
summary: This method replaces the manual, months-long conversion of hundreds of Linux kernel drivers when an API changes, specifically substituting hand-written Coccinelle semantic patches with a guided generation framework that decomposes examples into change variants, applies deterministic repairs, and uses a compile critic. It costs the implementation complexity of a script-based decomposer, SmPL syntax repair components, and a compilation feedback loop, requiring a domain-specific toolchain (Coccinelle) and incurring the latency of iterative generation and compilation for each variant. It can fail when general-purpose models produce weak results even with guidance (at most 12 solved), when the greedy rule composition misses correct combinations, or when the deterministic name generalisation fails to abstract driver-specific identifiers correctly.
rationale: This is a highly specialized framework for Linux kernel maintenance that requires the Coccinelle toolchain and domain-specific decomposition scripts, making it unsuitable for general production adoption without that specific workload.
technique: Guided decomposition for semantic patch generation

claims.statement: This method replaces the manual, months-long conversion of hundreds of Linux kernel drivers when an API changes, specifically substituting hand-written Coccinelle semantic patches with a guided generation framework that decomposes examples into change variants, applies deterministic repairs, and uses a compile critic. It costs the implementation complexity of a script-based decomposer, SmPL syntax repair components, and a compilation feedback loop, requiring a domain-specific toolchain (Coccinelle) and incurring the latency of iterative generation and compilation for each variant. It can fail when general-purpose models produce weak results even with guidance (at most 12 solved), when the greedy rule composition misses correct combinations, or when the deterministic name generalisation fails to abstract driver-specific identifiers correctly.

Qwen2.5-Coder 7B with the framework solves 35.3 conversions on average (range 32-41) against 1.0 when prompted directly, with rules that are the most precise on the test set (0.74 of changed files solved, against 0.55 for Spinfer and 0.70 for the frontier agent); the compile critic removes every output that matches the human fix but does not build.
